 Open Navigation Menu Menu Film 26 Contenders To Play The Next Bond Villain
 By Radhika Seth 18 November 2026 Getty Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Now that Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond and chatter is turning to who might play the next generation of Bond women , it’s also worth considering who our martini-swilling super spy will be facing off against in his next mission. From Javier Bardem to Rami Malek, Christoph Waltz to Mads Mikkelsen, some of the biggest names in Hollywood and beyond have taken these plum parts in recent years. Here are 26 contenders who could feasibly join them.
 Who Will Be The Next Generation Of Bond Girls? Here Are 45 Contenders Gallery 45 Photos By Radhika Seth View Gallery Michael Buckner/Getty Images 1/26 Native Share Timothée Chalamet 
 Hear me out: the four-time Oscar nominee will be the hero to Robert Pattinson’s villain in Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming Dune: Part Three , so why not flip the roles and order a rematch in the next Bond movie?
 Jeff Spicer/Getty Images 2/26 Native Share Jason Momoa 
 If you’re after someone with more, er, heft, might I suggest the hulking action star?
 Victor LOCHON/Getty Images 3/26 Native Share Stellan Skarsgård 
 I promise I will soon leave the Dune universe, but before I do, it’s worth saying that the Swedish acting legend feels like a no-brainer – he has the gravitas, can be menacing when required, and has delivered knockout performances in everything from Sentimental Value to Chernobyl .
 CHRIS DELMAS/Getty Images 4/26 Native Share Alexander Skarsgård 
 And if not the father, how about the son? The star of Succession and Big Little Lies has a penchant for playing delicious villains – and just think of the press tour fashion he’d bring to the table.
 Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images 5/26 Native Share Peter Dinklage 
 Alexander Skarsgård’s Wicker co-star, the four-time Emmy-winning Game of Thrones breakout, would also be an excellent choice.
 Dominik Bindl 6/26 Native Share John Malkovich 
 On the awards trail this season for his brilliant performance in Wild Horse Nine , it’s a wonder the 72-year-old has never played a Bond villain before.
 TheStewartofNY 7/26 Native Share Mahershala Ali 
 No one could be better than the suave double Oscar winner, who recently proved his action hero chops in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother .
 Theo Wargo/Getty Images 8/26 Native Share Cillian Murphy 
 Given Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight is penning the next Bond script, the Irish Oscar winner ought to be at the front of the queue.
 Karwai Tang 9/26 Native Share Sandra Hüller 
 Wouldn’t the beloved, Academy Award-nominated German star of Anatomy of a Fall , Zone of Interest , Rose , Project Hail Mary and Fatherland make a formidable, deadpan Bond villain? Not many women have had the honour of being the central antagonist in a Bond movie, but Hüller could certainly pull it off.
 Lyvans Boolaky/Getty Images 10/26 Native Share Charles Melton 
 He dazzled in May December , Warfare , Beef and the recent Her Private Hell – the rapidly rising star is someone the Bond franchise should snap up as soon as possible.
 Kristina Bumphrey/Getty Images 11/26 Native Share Jeremy Strong 
 From Succession ’s Kendall Roy, to The Apprentice ’s Roy Cohn, to The Social Reckoning ’s Mark Zuckerberg, the deeply committed Oscar nominee has made a career out of playing terrifying men in suits – becoming a fully-fledged Bond villain is the logical next step.
 John Lamparski 12/26 Native Share Michael B Jordan 
 He won an Oscar for Sinners , is about to direct himself in a reboot of The Thomas Crown Affair , and was the Black Panther franchise’s iconic super villain, Erik Killmonger – the heartthrob has the looks, physicality and talent to take on Pattinson.
 CHRIS DELMAS/Getty Images 13/26 Native Share Pedro Pascal 
 The zaddy of Game of Thrones and The Last of Us fame feels primed for a part like this – and is another actor who’d relish the press tour method dressing.
 Taylor Hill 14/26 Native Share Cate Blanchett 
 She’s one of the biggest names in the industry, with two Oscars under her belt, and has had a lot of fun playing frosty villains of late – just see: Tár , Don’t Look Up and Mrs America . The supremely accomplished Australian would be a highbrow choice.
 Karwai Tang 15/26 Native Share Ewan Mitchell 
 In House of the Dragon , the Brit (also seen in Saltburn and Wuthering Heights ) is the intensely creepy, long-haired, eyepatch-wearing Aemond Targaryen – perfect practice for playing a cat-stroking Bond villain, if you ask us.
 Mathew Tsang/Getty Images 16/26 Native Share Hudson Williams 
 A Canadian, like director Denis Villeneuve, the pin-up hit the big leagues with Heated Rivalry , and has legions of fans obsessed with his every move, onscreen and otherwise. He doesn’t need the Bond franchise, but it, arguably, needs him to secure its Gen-Z viewership.
 Julien Hekimian/Getty Images 17/26 Native Share Isabelle Huppert 
 Or would the francophone Villeneuve want to cast the 73-year-old French legend ( The Piano Teacher , Elle )? She’s razor-sharp, no-nonsense and would make a fearsome opponent for Bond.
 CHRIS DELMAS/Getty Images 18/26 Native Share Yura Borisov 
 The Russian who came from left field to score an Oscar nod for Anora , and will soon be seen alongside Andrew Garfield in Artificial , is a great actor and very much in that critically-acclaimed, international-leaning, Hollywood-recognised mould of recent Bond villains.
 Frazer Harrison/Getty Images 19/26 Native Share Daniel Kaluuya 
 It’s a shame he missed out on the part of Bond himself, but the next best thing would be for the Oscar-winning Londoner – who, lest we forget, worked with Villeneuve on the unbelievably tense thriller Sicario – to square up to Pattinson. From Get Out to Widows , Judas and the Black Messiah to Nope , he remains one of the best actors of his generation.
 Amy Sussman 20/26 Native Share Riz Ahmed 
 This is another Brit we could have seen as 007 – his latest TV show, Bait , is literally about an actor auditioning to be Bond. Renowned for his work in The Night Of , Four Lions , Sound of Metal and Mogul Mowgli , he’d make an excellent villain at the very least.
 Monica Schipper/Getty Images 21/26 Native Share Nicole Kidman 
 The Australian Academy Award winner never stops working and has been bouncing between genres of late – from procedurals ( Lioness , Scarpetta ) to quirky comedies ( Margo’s Got Money Troubles ) to legacy sequels ( Practical Magic 2 ). Why would a Bond movie be off the table? I can easily see her bringing the same unhinged energy that she channels in, say, Nine Perfect Strangers or The Northman to this franchise.
 Taylor Hill 22/26 Native Share Wagner Moura 
 Post Narcos , The Secret Agent brought the Brazilian to even greater prominence, by way of a Golden Globe win and an Oscar nomination. He’s dashing, to be sure, but can play conniving just as easily.
 John Nacion 23/26 Native Share Willem Dafoe 
 How on earth is the industry veteran ( The Florida Project , Poor Things , Nosferatu ) still yet to play a Bond villain? It’s an added bonus that coming on board would mean reuniting with his The Lighthouse co-star Robert Pattinson.
 Han Myung-Gu 24/26 Native Share Tilda Swinton 
 With her otherworldly style, impeccable acting and habit of embodying unforgettable villains (go watch Snowpiercer , Narnia , Okja , Suspiria and Michael Clayton ), the London-born powerhouse would be an inspired pick.
 Amy Sussman 25/26 Native Share Glenn Close 
 Another Hollywood fixture who’s never been afraid of dabbling in darker roles – Fatal Attraction , Dangerous Liaisons , 101 Dalmatians , The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping – is the eight-time Oscar-nominated 79 year old. Pattinson surely wouldn’t stand a chance against her character’s nefarious schemes.
 Taylor Hill 26/26 Native Share Kieran Culkin 
 Jeremy Strong’s fellow Roy brother from Succession – who memorably pipped his co-star to the post at the 2025 Oscars with his scene-stealing turn in A Real Pain – would make for a very enjoyable, wisecracking super villain. Bring on the zippy, improvised one-liners.
